answer: Canary leak checks: each identity's challenge hides a private decoy word that only it receives and must never use. Farms save money by packing many clones into one shared prompt, so decoys creep across like a vine over a fence: when B's text carries A's decoy, they share a pipeline and both forfeit the epoch. Assuming $0.002 per packed answer and $0.02 per isolated session, a 500-clone farm's bill climbs from $1 to $10 an epoch. Honest agents feel no change in their reward pulse; a violet decoy meant for someone else never reaches them, so it can't leak.
